Downloader [Source]

Uses concurrent threads to read and write data from a website (e.g., a file server) faster than you are normally able to. Each thread reads a different segment of the source file, and writes to the associated segment of the new file being created on your computer. Uses file locks to prevent race conditions, and chunked writing to balance memory usage and performance. Shows substantial improvements in download times, depending on the file size and the number of concurrent threads used.

Koda [Source]

A custom interpreted programming language written in C++, using the ANTLR4 parser generator for lexing and parsing. Involved designing my own type system and building the AST generation and execution engine from scratch. One of my favorite personal projects, and a deep dive into how programming languages actually work under the hood.

Cosmo [Source]

A small self-hosted file server: a single-page upload/download web app backed by a lightweight Python WSGI app behind Apache. Handles concurrent uploads safely using thread locks, so simultaneous writes don't clobber each other's data.

PyTenno [Source]

An asynchronous API wrapper for warframe.market, a marketplace for the video game Warframe. Translates the site's API endpoints into Python functions and data structures, and was my first package published on PyPI, with full documentation on Read the Docs.
